---
title: "Using AI in the Analysis of Marine Ecological Data"
---

A half-day, hands-on workshop on three complementary ways to use AI in an
analytical workflow — from lowest to highest commitment — worked end to end on
a single dataset: seven days of DCL/DE detections of North Atlantic right whale
up-calls.

- **Tier 1 — a chat interface**, for planning an analysis and reasoning about
  which model suits the data. Posit Assistant's `/plan` mode writes the plan to
  a file.
- **Tier 2 — a coding assistant** working alongside you in a live R session,
  in Positron or RStudio:
  exploratory analysis, environmental covariates from a remote API, and a
  log-Gaussian Cox process with self-excitement.
- **Tier 3 — a command-line agent** (`pa`) turned loose on a real repository:
  implementation, refactoring, manuscript documentation, and project tracking.

All three tiers are the same product — [Posit Assistant](https://assistant.posit.co),
in the editor, the IDE and the terminal — so moving up a tier changes how much
autonomy you grant, not which tool you use. Access is through Posit AI Pass:
one sign-in, no API keys.

We close with a look at running a local model via Ollama, for when data
privacy, cloud access or cost is a barrier.

Throughout, we weigh best practices and pitfalls, emphasising critical,
reproducible use: the AI accelerates the work, but you remain the scientist.

Intended for researchers with basic R familiarity. No AI experience required.
